title: Riding mower or lawn tractor: safe teardown
summary: A riding mower or lawn tractor gives a vertical-shaft petrol engine with its starter and charging stator, a 12 V battery, a starter solenoid, belts, pulleys, spindle bearings, switches and lights. Empty the fuel, pull the plug leads and take the battery off negative first before you touch a blade, and slide the deck out from the side: never work under the machine or trust a jack to hold it.

steps.text: Park on level, hard ground outdoors, away from flames, sparks and drains. Set the parking brake, switch the blades off and chock the wheels. Leave the key in until the engine run in step 2 is done; it comes out in step 3. Have an extinguisher or a bucket of sand to hand, and no smoking (safety_fuel_handling).
steps.warn: With the freewheel or bypass levers open the machine rolls freely, and Toro warns it could move unintentionally (Toro 75748 manual). Keep the wheels chocked the whole time.

steps.text: Empty the fuel. Pump the tank out into a fuel can with a hand pump (Toro 75748 manual). If the engine still runs, leave a little in, start it with the blades off and the parking brake on, and let it run until it stops: that empties the fuel lines and carburettor and proves the engine runs (Husqvarna YTH18542 manual). Then turn off the fuel shut-off valve if the fuel line has one.
steps.warn: Never start a siphon by mouth. Run the engine only in open air, never in a garage or shed: the exhaust holds carbon monoxide (safety_carbon_monoxide). Toro says not to drain fuel indoors or in a closed trailer.

steps.text: Let the engine and muffler cool until you can hold the back of your hand close to them and feel no warmth, and only then touch them. Pull the lead off each spark plug (two on a V-twin) and tuck it where it can't touch the plug (Husqvarna YTH18542 manual, Toro 75748 manual). Keep the key in your pocket.
steps.warn: Turning a blade or pulley turns the engine. With a lead on, it can fire.

steps.text: Take out the starting battery. Lift the seat or hood, undo the negative (black) cable first, then the positive (red), undo the hold-down and lift the battery out upright (Toro 75748 manual, Husqvarna YTH18542 manual). Wear glasses and gloves (safety_lead_acid).
steps.warn: Don't let a tool or a terminal touch the frame while the positive is still on: the spark can make the battery's gas explode (Toro 75748 manual).

steps.text: Drain the engine oil into a container while it is warm, not hot. The Husqvarna has a drain valve with a drain tube that fits on its fitting (Husqvarna YTH18542 manual); other engines vary, so find yours before you start. Seal and label the used oil. Don't pour it on the ground or down a drain.
Take off the hood: unplug the headlight connector, tilt the hood toward the engine and lift it off (Husqvarna YTH18542 manual). The headlight bulb holders pull out of the back of the grille.

Take the deck out from under the machine. Lower the deck lift lever to its lowest. On the Husqvarna, roll the deck belt off the engine pulley and unhook the clutch cable spring first. On both, pull the retainer springs or hairpin cotters and unhook the front link (the Toro's front support rod) and the lift links or arms on both sides. Then slide the deck out: to the right on the Husqvarna; on the Toro, rearward to free the belt, then out from under the machine (Husqvarna YTH18542 manual, Toro 75748 manual).
steps.warn: Once the links are off, the lift lever is spring-loaded: hold it firmly (Husqvarna YTH18542 manual). Never crawl or reach under the machine. The deck is heavy and awkward: take it with a helper. Never trust a jack alone: Toro says to use jack stands whenever it is raised.

steps.text: With a helper, turn the deck over onto cardboard, blades up. Wear thick gloves or wrap the blade in a rag, wedge a block of wood against it, and undo each blade bolt anticlockwise (Husqvarna YTH18542 manual, Toro 75748 manual). Keep each bolt and its washer with its blade.
steps.warn: On a deck with two or more blades, turning one blade turns the others (Toro 75748 manual). The bolts are tight: 62–75 N·m (45–55 ft-lb) on the Husqvarna, 81–108 N·m (60–80 ft-lb) on the Toro: brace so your hand can't slide onto an edge.

steps.text: Unhook the deck idler spring with a spring-removal tool (Toro uses one) and roll the deck belt off. Then unbolt the pulleys, idlers and blade spindles. Each spindle on the Toro holds two ball bearings (Toro 75748 manual, Toro 75748 parts).
steps.warn: The idler spring is under tension and can snap back (Toro 75748 manual). Wear safety glasses and keep your face and fingers out of its line.

steps.text: Put a tape label on each wire, then take the electrical parts: the starter solenoid, the fuse holder and blade fuses, the ignition, blade (PTO) and seat switches, and the wiring harness (Toro 75748 parts, Husqvarna YTH18542 manual).

Free the engine. Unhook the throttle cable and the engine's wiring plug, and close the fuel shut-off valve or clamp the fuel hose shut with a hose clamp, then pull the hose off with a rag under it. Roll the drive belt off the engine pulley and its idlers (Husqvarna YTH18542 manual). On machines with an electric blade clutch, take it off with the engine pulley; the Toro lists the two together (Toro 75748 parts). Then find and undo the engine's mounting bolts; their number and place vary by model.
steps.warn: A little fuel can still drip from the hose and carburettor. No sparks or flames nearby.

steps.text: Lift the engine out with a helper, straight up and kept upright, and set it on a pallet or blocks so the crankshaft end hangs free (safety_lifting).
steps.warn: Lift with your legs, keep your back straight, and keep fingers out from under it as it clears the frame.

steps.text: Take the seat with its switch, and the steel frame if you need it. To take a wheel off, raise that corner and set the frame on jack stands or solid blocks first: Toro says never to rely on a jack alone (Toro 75748 manual). Keep every part of you out from under it. Leave the transaxle where it is unless you have a use for it whole (see notes).

Store the engine upright under cover. Take out the spark plug, pour about 30 ml (1 fl oz) of engine oil into the cylinder, turn the engine over slowly a few times and refit the plug (Husqvarna YTH18542 manual, Toro 75748 manual). The crankcase is empty after step 5: refill it before you run the engine.

notes:
## What's worth keeping and why

- **The whole machine, if it runs.** A running tractor with a proper hitch pulls a trailer of firewood, water or tools. Tow only with a hitch made for towing and within the maker's weight limits; on slopes a towed load can cost you traction and control (Husqvarna YTH18542 manual). Strip it only when it is beyond use.
- **Engine.** A vertical-shaft petrol engine. The Husqvarna YTH18542 has a one-cylinder Briggs & Stratton Intek of 32.9 cu in (Husqvarna YTH18542 page); the Toro 75748 a 15.5 hp, 500 cc Briggs & Stratton (Toro 75748 page). The crankshaft points down, so take power off a pulley on its lower end with a belt, to a pump or a generator head, with the engine mounted the same way up (see teardown_gas_mower). Keep the spark plug type and gap from the manual or old plug: Champion XC92YC gapped 0.76 mm (0.030 in) on the Husqvarna (Husqvarna YTH18542 manual).
- **Charging stator.** On the Husqvarna it gives 3 A to the battery and 5 A to the headlights (Husqvarna YTH18542 manual). Leave it under the flywheel: it only works with the engine running, and then the engine is a slow 12 V battery charger.
- **Starter motor.** A 12 V DC motor made for short bursts: Toro says to crank for no more than 5 seconds at a time, Husqvarna no more than 15 seconds a minute (Toro 75748 manual, Husqvarna YTH18542 manual). Leave it on the engine unless you need it.
- **Battery.** A 12 V starting battery: the Husqvarna calls for 28 Ah, at least 230 cold-cranking amps, case size U1R; the Toro takes a 12 V, 230 CCA battery (Husqvarna YTH18542 manual, Toro 75748 parts). Both makers charge it at 6–10 A for an hour (Husqvarna YTH18542 manual, Toro 75748 manual). Charge it in an open, well-ventilated place away from sparks and flames, and unplug the charger before you connect or disconnect the leads: batteries give off explosive gas (Toro 75748 manual, Husqvarna YTH18542 manual; see safety_lead_acid). Toro stores it full, rechecks after 24 hours and recharges if it rests below 12.6 V (Toro 75748 manual). Good for lights, radios and small 12 V loads (build_led_lighting_12v, test_lead_acid).
- **Starter solenoid.** The switch that carries the starter's heavy current; the Toro lists one, 117-1197 (Toro 75748 parts). Reuse it to switch other heavy 12 V loads.
- **Electric blade clutch.** The Toro 75748 has one, part 117-7468, with its engine pulley (Toro 75748 parts). It works off the machine's battery; the blade-control (PTO) switch starts and stops the blades (Toro 75748 manual).
- **Belts, pulleys and idlers.** The Deere E100 guide lists a traction belt 2,492 mm long and a deck V-belt 2,635 mm long (Deere E100 parts). The Husqvarna's motion belt runs round the engine pulley, the transmission input pulley and three idlers (Husqvarna YTH18542 manual). Use them for line shafts and generator drives.
- **Bearings, switches, fuses and lights.** Deck spindle bearings (Toro 75748 parts); a 20 A blade fuse on the Husqvarna, 15 A and 25 A on the Toro (Husqvarna YTH18542 manual, Toro 75748 parts); a 27 W headlight bulb on the Deere (Deere E100 parts).
- **Fuel and oil.** Tanks hold 9.46 L (2.5 gal) on the Husqvarna and 11.4 L (3 gal) on the Toro (Husqvarna YTH18542 manual, Toro 75748 page). Engines take about 1.4 L of oil with the filter (Husqvarna YTH18542 manual, Deere E100 parts). Judge old fuel as in safety_fuel_handling.

## Variations

- **Husqvarna YTH18542:** 42 in lawn tractor with a Tuff Torq hydrostatic transmission and a freewheel control for pushing it by hand. The deck slides out from the right side (Husqvarna YTH18542 page, Husqvarna YTH18542 manual).
- **John Deere E100:** a General Transmission RT400 belt-driven CVT (TractorData E100). Deere's parts guide lists battery TY25221B (12 V), ignition switch GY20074 and the two belts above (Deere E100 parts).
- **Toro TimeCutter 75748:** a zero-turn with two blades and two hydro transaxles, one per rear wheel (Toro 75748 page, Toro 75748 parts). Its manual gives the weight as 218 kg (480 lb), but the Toro product page lists 299 kg (660 lb), so plan any lift for the heavier figure (Toro 75748 manual, Toro 75748 page). To push it, you open two bypass levers and put the key in RUN, because the electric brake needs a charged battery to let go (Toro 75748 manual).
- V-twin engines have two spark plugs and two leads. Engine makes, bolt layouts and where the battery sits vary: check yours as you go.

## What to leave

- **Hydrostatic transaxles.** Self-contained hydraulic drives: each Toro one holds a pump block, a cylinder block, a filter and an expansion tank (Toro 75748 parts). Heavy and hard to use away from the machine.
- **The flywheel and stator.** Leave them inside the engine.
- **Stale fuel and used oil.** Never pour them on the ground or into drains.
- The plastic hood and the deck shell, unless you need steel sheet.

## Testing what you got out

- **Engine:** step 2 is the test.
- **Charging:** before you strip a running machine, turn the headlights on, then shut the engine off. If the lights dim when it stops, the charging system was working (Briggs charging test).
- **Battery:** test_lead_acid. A charged battery rested for 24 hours should read 12.6 V or more (Toro 75748 manual).
- **Belts:** squealing, frayed edges, burn marks and cracks mean a worn belt (Toro 75748 manual).
